title: Vermillion Private Systems
text:
Vermillion Private Systems

notes:
- Account: Vermillion is a mid-stage healthtech platform managing PHI across EU subsidiaries. They treat any inference output as in-scope for residency and retention policies.
- Primary ask: Private VPC deployment with strict network controls. Must meet security review and legal residency, and integrate with their central KMS/HSM for per-customer keying.
- Network preference: Security team prefers AWS PrivateLink endpoints into Redwood control plane over simple VPC peering. Rationale: no route propagation, easier enforcement of egress controls, and aligns with their hub-and-spoke networking. Quote from lead infra sec: "traffic must never transit public internet or cross AZ boundaries in a way we can't monitor".
- Firewall / egress controls: Need explicit outbound allowlist for platform egress (list of static IPs or NAT gateway ranges) and ability to enforce egress via customer-managed NAT/egress gateways. They asked for a persistent outbound IP option or documented approach for customer NAT to present consistent source IPs.
- IP allowlists: Will require a short list of Redwood-managed egress IP ranges for PrivateLink endpoints; they want IPv4/IPv6 blocks and SLA on change windows (30d notice).
- Mutual TLS & mTLS: Request for mutual TLS between Redwood edge and customer VPC endpoints for stronger auth, plus support for client cert rotation.
- KMS integration: Must support customer-managed keys (CMK) in their AWS account with HSM-backed key material; Redwood must demonstrate envelope encryption and key usage audit logs. Legal flagged requirement: "Redwood must not hold plaintext root keys or have ability to export CMKs".
- Audit logging / SIEM: They require forwarding of inference audit logs and access events to their Splunk instance (syslog/S3 sink) and 1-year retention for logs; Redwood to provide schema for logs, retention policy, and proof of tamper-evidence (signed logs).
- Data residency & storage: All persistent artifacts (logs, KV caches, user-uploaded context) must remain in EU regions. Temporary runtime caches may exist on GPUs but must not be written to persistent storage outside EU.
- Model routing / fallback: They want primary hosted model in EU with on-failover rules to a secondary EU-only fallback model (no cross-region failover). Also asked about quantization profiles and performance tradeoffs for high-throughput embedding jobs.
- Latency / throughput targets: P99 < 200ms for chat median length (context ~1k tokens) for customer-facing assistant; embeddings pipeline expected 100 qps burstable to 300 for batch windows. Cost sensitivity moderate — prefer efficient batching + caching suggestions from Redwood Optimize.
- Security review: Vermillion will run Redwood through internal vendor security review (questionnaire + SOC2 + ISO27001 artifacts). They also require a short threat model doc and network runbook for their security team.
- POC plan: 2-week POC inside Vermillion VPC using PrivateLink; objectives: validate PrivateLink connectivity, persistent outbound IP approach, CMK envelope flow, and log forwarding to Splunk. Success criteria: 1) mTLS handshake validated, 2) CMK encrypt/decrypt operations logged, 3) logs visible in Splunk with required fields, 4) <200ms p99 chat latency at 50 qps.
- Pricing / contract: Legal requested a clause on key custody and data residency. Procurement asked for an estimate for Dedicated GPUs behind Private deployment (monthly). Forecasting to Q2 2026 if POC successful.
- Quotes / paraphrases: "We cannot tolerate any service that defaults to cross-border processing without explicit controls."
- Misc: A dev lead asked about PrivateLink peering alternatives: if customer wants on-prem -> Redwood to propose VPN + PrivateLink hybrid. Also asked about automated IP rotation windows and notification process.
- Action items: Redwood to deliver: (1) PrivateLink architecture diagram + CF/Terraform snippet, (2) egress IP ranges and change policy, (3) KMS integration design & keys ops runbook, (4) log schema + Splunk forwarding guide, (5) POC success checklist and estimate.
- Owner notes: AE Sofia to sync with Liam (SE) and Solutions (Priya) to finalize workshop agenda.


timeline:
2026-01-15: Intro call (Sofia). High level requirements captured: VPC-only, EU residency, per-customer keys.
2026-02-05: Security deep-dive with infra sec (Liam). Prefers PrivateLink over VPC peering for hub-and-spoke policy.
2026-02-28: Shared initial network checklist and sample CloudFormation/Terraform outputs.
2026-03-02: Architecture workshop (recording ff_20260302_vm-meeting-1229). Action: Redwood to produce PrivateLink design + egress control options.
2026-03-05: Legal raised addendum request for KMS HSM usage and customer-managed keys.
Planned 2026-03-22: On-site / virtual proof-of-concept kickoff (two-week POC).

next_step:
Share VPC network design template + AWS PrivateLink architecture diagram; schedule architecture workshop week of 2026-03-22

blockers:
legal: final list of EU data residency countries
security: need accepted private connectivity pattern (PrivateLink vs peering)
ops: persistent outbound IPs for IP allowlist not confirmed
procurement: contract redlines on KMS/HSM key usage
